_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies". A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn. "cue" is when the talk comes on: "start" as the lesson opens, {"after": "<figure>"} once that figure's task is done, or "check" as the final check opens. "locals" names who in town asked a forecast question, by the forecast's "id" in the lesson file.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. You sound cheerful. Did Edna get her picnic?

replies.say: Dry, no tent. She shook my hand.
replies.back: Edna Pruitt shook your hand? I’ve known her twenty years and only ever got a nod. You’re made.

replies.say: We put the tent up, and it didn’t rain.
replies.back: That’s what the lesson said: a grey sheet without depth stays dry. Still, Edna will call the tent prudence, which in her book is the highest praise.

turns.them: Now listen. Hap Delaney came on the air from Pasco yesterday. He has the afternoon mail run, and he wants to know how to tell from the morning sky whether he’ll be flying into rain by afternoon. And Miss Abernathy’s Sunday school class has sent a note asking how high the clouds are. Twenty-two children are waiting on your answer.

replies.say: How high? How would anybody know that?
replies.back: With a balloon, an aeroplane, or your own hand. Two of those are expensive.

replies.say: Hap could just look out the window.
replies.back: Hap looks out the window plenty. He just doesn’t know what he’s looking at.

turns.them: This week, the middle floor: the hardest to read and the most useful to know. And bring your hands. You’ll need both.
Quick. A layer of lumps high in the sky, and each lump is wider than three fingers held at arm’s length. Which floor?

replies.back: Right. Big lumps are close lumps. Wider than three fingers, it’s low.
Altocumulus lumps sit between a little fingernail and three fingers. Wider than three fingers is the low floor: stratocumulus.
Cirrocumulus grains are smaller than your little fingernail. Wider than three fingers is low: stratocumulus.

turns.them: Hap tried this once with his whole arm out of the cockpit. Lost a glove over Ritzville.

replies.back: A farmer did. Mailed it back, postage due.

turns.them: You’re at the frosted glass now, and the sun is a pale disc. Look at the ground. What’s missing?

replies.back: Gone, because the light comes from the whole sky instead of one bright sun. That’s altostratus.
The birds are fine. Look down: no shadows. The light comes from the whole sky at once.
The goat. We’ve been over this. And the shadows are gone too: the light comes from the whole sky.

turns.them: When that frosted glass keeps thickening, nobody should plan a picnic. You know who to tell.
Every floor called on the club’s photographs. Now answer Hap and the Sunday school, in that order. Hap’s the one with an aeroplane.
